summary: Backend-only testing of StreamHub API. All 25 pytest cases passed (100% success), covering auth, categories, video upload + FFmpeg transcode (waited for status=ready with 10 thumbnails and 2+ renditions), views/likes, recommendations, comments CRUD, video update/delete, packages CRUD, announcements, admin stats/users/ban-unban/role/settings, profile avatar/cover uploads, Stripe checkout + payment status, and email verification toggle flow.

minor.issue: No idempotency / no auth check; views can be incremented infinitely from any client. Consider rate limiting or per-user uniqueness.
Accept untyped dict payload (no Pydantic validation). Should use typed request models.
Admin can demote themselves and lock out all admins; consider safeguard.
Runs `git pull` via subprocess on /app with no auth on git remote; potential security concern in production.

action_items: Consider auth/rate-limit on POST /api/videos/{id}/view to prevent abuse.
Add typed Pydantic models for category/package/announcement create payloads instead of raw dict.
Add safeguard so the last admin cannot demote themselves via /api/admin/users/{id}/role.
Note: log line in server.py startup says 'admin@streamhub.local' but seeded email is 'admin@streamhub.io' (minor log message mismatch).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~950 lines; consider splitting into routers (auth, videos, admin, payments) for maintainability.
Stripe webhook signature verification relies on emergentintegrations.handle_webhook; ensure it actually validates the signature.
process_video catches BLE001 broadly; OK for background, but failed transcodes never clean up partial files/thumbnails.
/api/users/me/avatar and /cover do not validate file type or size; an attacker could upload arbitrary files.
/api/videos/upload reads in 1MB chunks but writes synchronously inside async handler (file.write blocks the loop).
seed_data_creation: Each run registers a unique test user (test_<uuid>@example.com) and a verification user (verify_<uuid>@example.com). Test category/package/announcement are created and deleted within tests. Test video is uploaded and deleted within tests.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All backend endpoints from the review request are tested and passing. FFmpeg transcode flow validated end-to-end (3s testsrc mp4 -> ready with 10 thumbnails + renditions in ~10s). Ban test re-enables the user via unban; email verification flag is restored to false in finally block. Stripe checkout uses emergentintegrations with sk_test_emergent from backend/.env and was verified to create a session and payment_transactions record (status endpoint returned 200).
rca of the issue: N/A - no bugs blocking the listed features.
